_comment: Whole-store refusal baseline for ACS-100i-7. Records the refusal messages that are NOT attributable to the top-level package-surface if/then rule. The guard test asserts this set is byte-identical: none added, none removed, no message changed. A shrunken set normally means validation was loosened generally instead of the trigger narrowed. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-01 at merge commit 1695b0ec, against the merged tree rather than either side's pre-merge number. Two baselines converged here. This branch widened test_spec's framework enum to name vitest AND playwright, and type to name component, in BOTH config/ac_store_schema.json and config/test_requirements.schema.json — taking the refusal set from 28 to 0. Concurrently and independently, origin/main widened framework to name playwright only, in ac_store_schema.json only, taking its own baseline from 28 to 26 — the 26 remaining being the records that declare vitest. The merge takes the superset, which is why the count here is 0 and not 26. The disappearance is a vocabulary repair, not a loosening: the pre-merge guard run reported Added: [] and Messages changed: [] — removals only. See KI-ACS-010. NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS NEXT: with an empty set the 'Removed' direction of the guard is now vacuous; the 'Added' direction still bites, and that is the direction that matters. Regenerate ONLY in a commit that can point at the record or schema edit explaining each removal; never to make a red assertion go green.

supersedes.reason: The common ancestor of both fixes. All 28 entries were test_spec framework/type enum refusals: 26 records declaring framework vitest, 2 declaring playwright, 9 of them also declaring type component.

origin/main's independent, narrower fix — playwright added to ac_store_schema.json alone. It resolved its 2 playwright records, left the 26 vitest ones refused, and left config/test_requirements.schema.json at [unittest, pytest], so a playwright AC would validate while generating a ticket that violates its own unenforced schema. Superseded by this branch's superset widening of both schemas.
